content.value_statement: Next.js code can fail when patterns drift across framework versions. This skill guides Claude and Codex with focused rules for App Router, RSC, data, assets, and deployment.
actual_capabilities: Reviews App Router file conventions, route handlers, parallel routes, and intercepting routes.
Explains safe React Server Component boundaries and common client component mistakes.
Recommends data fetching patterns for Server Components, Server Actions, Route Handlers, and client components.
Guides metadata, Open Graph image, image optimization, font optimization, and script loading choices.
Covers self-hosting setup, cache handlers, Docker output, and debugging workflows.
limitations: Does not run tests or inspect a project unless the assistant separately reads the project files.
Does not replace official Next.js release notes for newly changed APIs.
Examples use placeholder services and must be adapted to the application security model.
Focuses on Next.js App Router patterns, not general React architecture.

use_cases.title: Review App Router Code
use_cases.description: Check a Next.js feature for route structure, async params, RSC boundaries, and route handler placement.

use_cases.title: Plan Data Fetching
use_cases.description: Choose between Server Components, Server Actions, Route Handlers, and client fetching for a feature.

use_cases.title: Prepare Self-Hosted Deployments
use_cases.description: Apply standalone output, container guidance, cache handler notes, and health check practices before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Check A Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one route or component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next.js page for App Router best practices. Focus on async params, server versus client components, and clear fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Data Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Select the right data flow for a feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this feature description, recommend the right Next.js data pattern. Compare Server Components, Server Actions, Route Handlers, and client fetching.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Production Issues
prompt_templates.scenario: Diagnose hydration, metadata, script, image, or bundle problems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Next.js issue and propose a fix using the skill rules. Include the likely cause, affected files, and a minimal change plan.

prompt_templates.title: Review Deployment Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this self-hosted Next.js deployment plan. Evaluate standalone output, cache handlers, image optimization, health checks, and runtime configuration.

output_examples.input: A client component is marked async and directly awaits data.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains that async client components are invalid, moves the fetch to a Server Component, and passes serializable props down.

output_examples.input: A team wants one endpoint for a mobile app and web form submissions.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends Route Handlers for external clients and Server Actions for UI mutations, with reasons for caching and progressive enhancement.

output_examples.input: A Docker deployment serves inconsistent ISR content across instances.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies local filesystem cache as the issue and recommends a shared cache handler with a deployment checklist.

best_practices: Start with Server Components for reads and use Client Components only for browser-only behavior.
Choose the smallest Next.js primitive that matches the workflow, then document the tradeoffs.
Validate deployment assumptions for cache, runtime configuration, image handling, and health checks.
anti_patterns: Adding use client to large route trees instead of isolating interactive components.
Using Route Handlers for internal UI mutations when Server Actions fit better.
Copying example domains, keys, or deployment commands without adapting them to the project.

faq.question: Does this skill support Next.js App Router?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on App Router conventions, Server Components, route handlers, metadata, and related APIs.

faq.question: Can it fix hydration errors?
faq.answer: It can guide diagnosis and suggest common fixes for browser APIs, dates, random values, invalid HTML, and scripts.

faq.question: Does it execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The host assistant controls whether any command is run.

faq.question: Can it review self-hosted deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers standalone output, Docker notes, cache handlers, runtime variables, and health checks.

faq.question: Is it only for Vercel deployments?
faq.answer: No. It includes Vercel-friendly patterns and specific guidance for deploying Next.js outside Vercel.

faq.question: Should I still check official Next.js docs?
faq.answer: Yes. Use official docs for version-specific changes, especially when upgrading to a newer Next.js release.
